guidance: The letters walk the route. The G3 set (remake: the only set) runs fence → cabin roof → branch → log → loader, the first half of the tape route; the A sits on the branch directly below the tape (VG PS2).
Cause and effect in view. The generator's effect is seen "in the distance": the loader rises and opens (G3 p045). The switch is a red box with a lever (J3).

The climb is a visible staircase. Loader, tower, covered half pipe and ramp stand one above the other at the far end of the forest; each next ramp is in view from the last (G3: "line up and ollie", "line up straight for the next jump").
Pickups reward the walkways. Stat points on the Horn rope and on the generator rope back towards the park bring players to the generator before they know what it does (G3 p048).
Hidden on purpose: the tape is behind the spawn and above the treetops; the cable up the cliff is not signposted (TAS only).
designLogic: First switch-gated tape. Canada (career 2) adds an unlock; the switch lies on the walkway everyone uses, and its effect is visible from it.
A staircase of transfers. Banked wall → loader → tower half pipe → covered half pipe → ramp → rail: each step is a vert transfer upward, so the climb converts vert skill into height.
Little overlap, high stakes. G3 warns there is "not much overlap" between loader and tower; the jumps are tuned to demand line-up and speed, and a miss falls 10–20 m.
State persists, so failure is affordable. The loader stays raised; LP3's failed first ascent cost ≈ 29 s and the second attempt still fitted in the run.
The letters are the rehearsal. The G3 set covers the route up to the climb; the remake keeps only that set and says "follow the same path as for the SKATE letters".
Tape at a fork, not a dead end. Right rail → tape → exit onto the Around the Horn rope (a goal); left rail → the level's longest grind (Mine Cart Ride, 500) and a launch back to the lot.
Exit into a goal. Both the TAS and LP3 chain the tape into Mountain Man Mine Stomp → Look Ma! No Talent! → Around the Horn: the tape's descent is the start of the treetop scoring line.
Behind the spawn. The spawn faces the lot; the tape lies behind and above, so it is found by turning round, the opposite of Foundry's tape over the middle.
Three areas, three letter tours. Each skater group's letters tour one area (lot, park, forest), so the level is learnt area by area across the cast.
Expert bypass. The TAS climbs a cable from the cabin roof up the cliff to the track in 8 s, skipping the switch: lines (ropes, cables) connect the layers for those who see them.
Difficulty step from Foundry. Foundry: no unlock, two leaps, ≈ 6–9 m. Canada: unlock + four transfers, ≈ 15–25 m, a rail choice.
The PS1 edition keeps the idea. A smaller, different layout still puts the tape at the top of a mine-cart track up the mountain (VG PS1).
The remake extends the branches. Cash and the Iron Galaxy logo on the left branch, COMBO at the foot of the climb, a man waiting by the raised quarter pipe (thermos goal): the climb becomes a hub.
remakeChanges: Tape: same route (lever → elevated half pipe → platforms → track; LP34 0:20:00-0:20:20)
Letters: three sets (lot, park, forest) -> forest set only, along the tape route
Goals: Melon Grab Over the Blade removed; Bury That Bully reworked (boneless to a platform, grind a short rail); High Combo 10,000; five pro goals
COMBO letters added at the raised loader (pro goal)
New pickups populate the other branch of the fork: Cash and the Iron Galaxy logo on the left track and wire; Hidden Deck under the flag; plushie; thermos errand
PS1 edition (2001): different layout and goals; tape at the top of a mine-cart track on the slope
transfer: Switch-raised ramp. A trick rail or lever on the walkway route that raises a quarter-pipe platform (moving platform) 4–6 m, visible from the switch; it stays up for the run.

Staircase of vert transfers. Three vert ramps at rising heights (each ≈ 3–4 m higher), linked by transfers/spine transfers; keep each landing deck ≥ 3 m deep on the near side so line-up, not luck, decides.
Crystal at a rail fork. At the top, a grindable track that splits: right branch carries the crystal, left branch is a long descending grind (travelling-rail feel) back towards the start.
Exit into a line. After the crystal, a short ollie from the rail's end onto a rope/rail circling a big tree, so the crystal run flows into a scoring line.
Letters as rehearsal. Put the level's lesser pickups along the lower half of the crystal route (fence, roof, branch, log, ramp).
Expert cable. A long grindable cable (snapping rope or travelling rail) from a roof near the spawn up a cliff to the track: fast for those who see it, risky (a fall ≥ 10 m).
Keep walkers off. The track ≥ 15 m above the forest floor with no standable ledge within the 4.6 m double-jump + ledge-grab reach.
